title: Oracle: OD-13 supersedes OD-5/R1001 (BL-14)
body:
Oracle ruling on the logged evidence `BL-14` (and `BL-13`), dispatched by the unattended delivery driver on base `run/web`.

**OD-13** — the owner's 2026-08-19 ruling overrules OD-5 on the whole-transcript cap. This decision supersedes `R1001` and adds `R1008`.

- `R1001` is retired, so the merged plan `docs/plans/oracle/capped-whole-transcript-path.md` must not be built as merged — all of its slices implement the reversed routing.
- `R1008` keeps the reporting half of `R1001`, so the routing the owner amended into `R28` stays observable at the checkpoint before anything is spent.
- `OD-4`/`R1000` is untouched, and its re-cut lands first: the ratio only routes honestly once each transcript character is counted once.

The handoff at `docs/oracle/handoff-2026-08-20-1.md` carries the steward's next step.

Opened by the server-side `open-pr` workflow at the driver's request: this session cannot mint App identity (the hosted platform's proxy owns the credential, ESC-50), and a pipeline pull request authored by the owner would hollow out `owner-authored.sh` and be unapprovable by its own author.
